Four photos of two things side by side with price cards: a red bag $20 and a black bag $80, a black watch $90 and a blue watch $10, a small cake $20 and a big cake $40, a red book $30 and a green book $10. Narrated; Ana says I want to buy the cheaper bag.

lesson.title: 5.11 The red bag is cheaper
lesson.unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
lesson.goal: Compare prices with cheaper than and more expensive than (The red bag is cheaper than the black bag. / The black watch is more expensive than the blue watch.) and answer Which bag is cheaper? The red one.
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.11 Buying Things: A1 says a thing is cheap or expensive; A1+ 5.11 compares two prices with A1+ 2.11's than: a short adjective takes -er (cheaper), and a long one takes more (more expensive), the one new relationship. Each photo shows two things of one kind side by side with their price cards, so every comparison is true of one photo only; a bank never offers the converse sentence that is also true (The black bag is more expensive than the red bag.). Which … is cheaper? is answered with A1+ 2.10's one. 5.6's want to comes back.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 5.11 cheap, expensive, buy; A1+ 2.11 -er than; A1+ 2.10 Which …? The red one.; A1 5.12 the tens; A1+ 5.6 want to.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say more expensive as one group with the stress on PEN (more ex-PEN-sive) and cheaper with CHEAP; do not require native-like speed.
